title: Postăvarul and the Bucegi: A Ski Week on the Prahova Valley
subRegion: Postăvarul massif and the Prahova Valley, Brașov & Prahova counties

bestPeriod.window: mid-January to late February — coldest air, best snowmaking window, full lift operation
bestPeriod.avoid: 26 December–7 January (Romanian holiday peak, DN1 gridlock) and any Saturday on the valley road

hook: Romania's ski country is one limestone massif and one big plateau, forty minutes apart, sharing a motorway-less valley and no joint lift pass. You get north-facing runs that hold snow, a gondola out of a spa town, a black under a cable car, castles on the rest day and *bulz* for lunch at a fraction of Alpine prices. What you do not get is a linked ski area or a short lift queue. Come knowing that, and it is very good value.

snapshot.Getting there: Bucharest Otopeni (OTP). Train Bucharest Nord → Brașov, then bus 20 to Poiana Brașov. Sinaia is on the same line, 1 h 40 from Bucharest. Driving means the DN1 — see the warning below.

itinerary.title: Bucharest to the Poiana
itinerary.morning: Land at Otopeni, transfer to Bucharest Nord, and take the InterRegio to Brașov — **around 2 h 30 to 3 h** on the fast services through the Prahova Valley, with the Bucegi wall out the left window from Sinaia onwards.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus **20** from Brașov's Livada Poștei up to **Poiana Brașov**, 20 minutes. Collect hire skis in the Poiana rather than in town; several shops sit at the gondola base and prices run €12–€18 a day [VERIFY: current rental rates].
itinerary.evening: Settle in, buy the pass for tomorrow at the base ticket office, and eat at **Coliba Haiducilor** — a log outlaw's-hut restaurant with an open fire, *ciorbă de burtă* and grilled meats.

itinerary.title: Learning the north face
itinerary.morning: First gondola. Warm up on **Bradul**, then move onto **Drumul Roșu** — the long blue back to the Poiana that gives you the whole vertical without the pitch, and the best way to read the mountain on day one.
itinerary.afternoon: Up the **Kanzel cable car** to the summit sector and take **Kanzel** itself, then **Sulinar**. Both hold their pitch a long way; if the top is windy, drop back to **Ruia**, which is sheltered by trees.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Casa Vânătorului** in the Poiana — game, *bulz* (mămăligă baked around melted sheep's cheese, sometimes with an egg and bacon), and a *țuică* to start.

itinerary.title: The Lupului day
itinerary.morning: **Lupului** — Poiana Brașov's serious run, taken early before the traffic. Repeat it while the surface is still cold and grippy; by 11:00 the sun has been on it.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski the top-station sector until the light flattens, then take an afternoon lesson or a guided half-day to learn the resort's tree lines. Poiana's ski schools are cheap by European standards and speak good English.
itinerary.evening: Bus down to **Brașov** for the evening. Eat at **Sergiana** on Strada Mureșenilor — a cellar restaurant doing the Transylvanian repertoire properly — then walk Piața Sfatului and the Black Church exterior under lights.

itinerary.title: Rest day: Peleș, Pelișor and Bran
itinerary.morning: Move base down the valley to **Sinaia** (train from Brașov, 45–60 min). Go straight to **Peleș Castle**, Carol I's 1873–1914 Neo-Renaissance royal residence, and the finest interior in Romania. Buy the ground-floor-plus-first-floor ticket, not the basic one [VERIFY: current Peleș ticket prices and winter opening days].
itinerary.afternoon: **Pelișor**, five minutes uphill — Queen Marie's smaller Art Nouveau house and, for many visitors, the better building of the two. Then, if the day allows, a taxi or bus to **Bran Castle** on the other side of the massif; it is a 90-minute run from Sinaia and better done from Brașov if you have the choice.
itinerary.evening: Sinaia. Dinner at **La Ceaun** on Bulevardul Carol I — cauldron-cooked stews, *tochitură*, big portions, low prices, always busy.

itinerary.title: Cota 1400 and Cota 2000
itinerary.morning: The gondola from Sinaia town, then up to **Cota 1400**. Warm up in the wooded sector, then continue to **Cota 2000** for the open Bucegi terrain — treeless, exposed, and a completely different mountain from Postăvarul.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski the **Carp** and the **Vânturiș**. Watch the wind: Cota 2000 shuts on high wind more often than any lift in Romania, and when it does the whole resort funnels into the 1400 sector.
itinerary.evening: Sinaia Casino and the Bulevardul Carol I promenade, then dinner in town. Check tomorrow's avalanche bulletin — Salvamont Prahova posts a Bucegi rating through the season.

itinerary.title: Touring the Bucegi plateau
itinerary.morning: Meet the guide at Cota 2000 with touring gear and transceiver. The plateau route heads north across the Bucegi towards **Babele** and the Sfinxul rock formations — rolling, wind-scoured, and enormous.
itinerary.afternoon: Depending on the bulletin, either continue towards **Vârful Omu (2,505 m)** or turn back and take the guided line into the **Valea Soarelui**. In stable conditions the Sun Valley is the best off-piste descent on the Prahova Valley; in unstable conditions it is where you do not go.
itinerary.evening: Back to Sinaia. Eat *cozonac secuiesc* — the Szekler chimney cake, better known as *kürtőskalács*, baked on a spit and rolled in sugar and walnut — from a street griddle, then a proper dinner.

itinerary.title: Predeal, Clăbucet, and out
itinerary.morning: Short train hop to **Predeal**, the highest town in Romania at around 1,040 m. Ski **Clăbucet** — the valley's best beginner and confidence terrain, wide and forgiving, and worth a morning even if you have been skiing all week.
itinerary.afternoon: If the group wants one more, **Azuga**'s Sorica sector is ten minutes further and almost always empty. Otherwise, train back to Bucharest from Predeal or Sinaia.
itinerary.evening: Bucharest. **Avoid driving the DN1 on a Sunday afternoon** at any cost — see the transport note. The train is immune to it.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Alpin / Poiana Brașov ski-in properties
accommodationStrategy.description: Poiana Brașov's hotels sit on or beside the piste with ski-in access, boot rooms and drying space, and a bus stop for Brașov at the door. Staying in the Poiana rather than Brașov saves you an hour of bus commute a day.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6–10 weeks ahead for January–February; Romanian school holidays fill it [VERIFY: current nightly rates].

accommodationStrategy.name: A guesthouse (*pensiune*) on Strada Furnica
accommodationStrategy.description: Furnica runs uphill from the town towards the gondola and the Peleș approach, so you are walking distance from both the lift and the castles, which is exactly the split this half of the week needs. Cheaper than any hotel on the boulevard.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–5 weeks ahead, direct or by platform; ask for a room away from the road.

accommodationStrategy.name: Cabana Mălăiești or a Bucegi cabana
accommodationStrategy.description: for the touring day, sleeping high removes the lift-dependence entirely and puts you on the plateau at first light. Basic, wood-heated, bookable direct.
accommodationStrategy.booking: by phone, 2–3 weeks ahead; confirm winter opening, as some Bucegi cabanas close or run reduced service [VERIFY: winter opening and rate].

logistics.connectivity: Excellent 4G/5G in Brașov, the Poiana, Sinaia and Predeal — Romanian mobile data is fast and cheap. Coverage on the Bucegi plateau is patchy in the valleys and good on the ridges.
logistics.emergency: **112**, and **Salvamont 0725 826 668**. Give the massif name (Postăvarul or Bucegi) and the piste or route name. Salvamont teams are unpaid-adjacent professionals and respond fast; do not use them as a taxi.
logistics.weather: The Bucegi plateau generates its own weather — Cota 2000 can be in full whiteout while Sinaia town is sunny. Wind closures on the upper Sinaia lifts are the single most common disruption. January inversions can leave the valley at −15 °C and the tops warmer.
logistics.bookingWindows: Accommodation 6–10 weeks for the January–February peak. Lift passes are bought on the day at the base office; there is no advantage to pre-buying. Guided touring 2–3 weeks.
logistics.money: Cards work at lift offices, hotels and most restaurants. Mountain cabanas, small rental shops and the *kürtőskalács* stalls are cash. Carry 300–500 RON (€57–€95). Prices here are quoted in lei; euro is not accepted at the lifts.
logistics.transportRules: The **Bucharest–Brașov train** is the smart arrival — 2 h 30 to 3 h on fast services, and it bypasses the road entirely. **The DN1 is the notorious problem**: it is the only road up the Prahova Valley, it is single carriageway through Comarnic and Sinaia, and Friday-evening and Sunday-afternoon queues out of and back into Bucharest routinely run three to five hours. If you drive, travel at unsociable hours and buy the **rovinietă** e-vignette — category A, 1 day €3.50 (~18 RON), 10 days €6 (~31 RON), 30 days €9.50 (~50 RON); there is no 7-day product. Winter tyres are legally required on snow- or ice-covered roads.
logistics.permits: No permits for the pisted resorts. The Bucegi Natural Park covers the plateau — stay on established touring routes and do not camp inside protected zones. Off-piste is not policed, which is not the same as safe: carry transceiver, shovel and probe on the plateau.

proTips: Ski **Sinaia midweek and Poiana Brașov at the weekend**, not the other way round. Sinaia's lift capacity is the bottleneck on the whole valley; Poiana absorbs a Saturday far better.
Take the **first gondola of the day at Sinaia**, around 08:30–09:00, and you skip the queue that defines the resort by 10:00 [VERIFY: current first-lift times].
Budget for **two separate lift passes**. There is no valley-wide product, and travellers who assume otherwise end up paying day rates twice.
Eat lunch on the mountain at 11:30 or 13:45, never at 12:30. Romanian ski restaurants fill in a single wave.
Learn *"o zi de schi"* (one ski day) and *"telecabina merge?"* (is the cable car running?). The second question is asked constantly on the Sinaia side and the answer changes hourly.
Do the castles on a **weekday**, not the weekend. Peleș on a Saturday in season is a queue in the cold; on a Wednesday you walk in.
If natural snow is thin, go straight to **Cota 2000** and Poiana's north face and ignore Predeal and Azuga entirely — altitude and aspect are doing all the work in a warm winter.

raw.Poiana Brașov (Postăvarul massif, 1,030–: Romania's best-organised resort: roughly 24 km of piste on the north face of Postăvarul, above the Poiana at 1,030 m and topping out at **Vârful Postăvarul, 1,799 m**. Key runs: the **Kanzel** and **Lupului** (Wolf) — the long, serious lines off the top, dropping the full vertical in one go; **Ruia** and **Sulinar**, the steeper mid-mountain reds; **Bradul** and **Drumul Roșu**, the blues that make the resort work for improvers, Drumul Roșu being the long, winding cruise back to the Poiana. Lifts: **two gondolas** from the Poiana plus the **Kanzel cable car** (*telecabina*) to the top station, with chairlifts and drags filling in. [VERIFY: current number of operating lifts and total piste km for 2026/27]
raw.Sinaia (Bucegi eastern flank, 800–2,000: Two distinct sectors: **Cota 1400**, the wooded mid-mountain, and **Cota 2000** on the open Bucegi shoulder — this is the highest lift-served skiing in Romania and the only place in the country with reliable alpine-zone snow. Named runs include the **Carp** and the **Vânturiș**, plus the long descent from Cota 1400 back towards town. A **gondola runs from Sinaia town itself** at around 800 m, so you can ski from the door. **Honest warning: Sinaia's lift infrastructure is its weak point.** The gondola and the Cota 1400–2000 link are chronically undersized for weekend demand and queues of 45–60 minutes on a Saturday are routine, not exceptional. Ski Sinaia midweek or accept the wait.
raw.Predeal (1,100–1,500 m): is the lowest resort on the valley and the iciest, sitting on a saddle with heavy exposure to thaw-freeze — but it has the valley's **best beginner terrain at Clăbucet**, wide, gentle and lift-served, and it is where Romanian ski schools take first-timers. **Azuga** is the small fourth option, with the Sorica sector and a quieter feel.
raw.Ski pass tiers — and the planning point: **There is no single interconnected pass across the Prahova Valley. Each resort sells its own** — Poiana Brașov, Sinaia, Predeal and Azuga are four separate tariffs with no joint product, no shared points system and no reciprocity. Budget for two passes across the week. Indicative recent pricing: Poiana Brașov 1-day adult around **€30–€38 (150–190 RON)**, 6-day around **€150–€185 (750–950 RON)**; Sinaia 1-day adult around **€28–€35 (140–175 RON)**, with the Cota 2000 sector sometimes ticketed separately; Predeal noticeably cheaper. **All of these figures need a current check before you budget** [VERIFY: 2026/27 Poiana Brașov tariff] [VERIFY: 2026/27 Sinaia tariff and whether Cota 2000 is a separate ticket] [VERIFY: 2026/27 Predeal and Azuga tariffs].
raw.Snow reliability: The season runs roughly **mid-December to March**, occasionally into early April at Cota 2000. Aspect decides everything here: **Postăvarul's runs face north and hold snow markedly better than Predeal's**, which sits lower and on a more exposed saddle. Every resort on the valley relies on **heavy snowmaking** — Poiana Brașov's system covers most of its pisted terrain and is the reason the resort opens reliably in December. Natural cover is thin below 1,200 m in a warm winter; do not book a February week on the assumption of powder.
raw.Ski touring and off-piste: The **Bucegi plateau** above Cota 2000 is the touring ground — the Babele and Omu approaches, the Jepii and the descent lines back east. The classic lift-accessed off-piste from the Sinaia side drops into the **Valea Soarelui** (Sun Valley), and it is avalanche terrain in a serious range, not a sidecountry lap. Go with a guide: **Salvamont Brașov** and **Salvamont Prahova** run the rescue side, and licensed mountain guides work through the Romanian Mountain Guides Association and Brașov-based operators such as Carpathian Travel Center and Alpine Adventure [VERIFY: current guided ski-touring day rate].
raw.Rescue: **Salvamont national dispatch 0725 826 668**, plus 112. Install the Salvamont and DSU apps before you travel — both give your GPS position to dispatch. Salvamont Brașov covers Postăvarul and the Piatra Craiului; Salvamont Prahova covers the Bucegi and the Sinaia sectors.
